classification.difficultyReason: Apply the sine rule and explain why the resulting sine value makes the given triangle impossible.

content.prompt: Try to find the angle $\theta$ in this triangle; explain why it is impossible.

spec.description: Unshaded schematic triangle with a horizontal base, upper vertex, both base-angle arcs, left side labelled 10, right side labelled 25, left angle theta and right angle 30 degrees. The intentionally inconsistent measurements are preserved; the sketch is not a scale construction.
spec.mathematics: The side opposite theta is 25 and the side opposite 30 degrees is 10. These givens require sin(theta)=1.25.
spec.answerVisibility: All diagram labels are permanent student givens.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{\sin\theta}{25}&=\frac{\sin30^{\circ}}{10}\\\sin\theta&=\frac{25\sin30^{\circ}}{10}\\\sin\theta&=\frac54=1.25\end{align*}$$
Since a sine value cannot exceed $1$, $\sin^{-1}(1.25)$ has no real value. Therefore, no such triangle can be constructed.
